label: India

parties.name: Samajwadi Party (with the RLD in 2004 and 2019)
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (2014, outside the UPA)
All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam

allocation.label: First past the post (543 constituencies, regional seats curve)

governmentText.majority: {party} governs with {seats} seats, a Lok Sabha majority its allies already helped build.
governmentText.confidence_supply: {lead} governs with outside support from {partner}, which backs the government without joining it.
governmentText.minority: {party} forms a minority government on {seats} seats and has to win its support vote by vote.
governmentText.hung: No front reaches 272. {largest} is the largest group, and the President waits to see who can show a majority.

goalHint: Reach {majority} of {total} seats. Alliances are fought state by state, so Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and the big southern and eastern states count as much as a sweep of the Hindi belt.

issues.name: Prices
issues.blurb: Food and fuel inflation, onion and pulse prices, and the rupee.

issues.name: Jobs
issues.blurb: Unemployment, short-term recruitment and a young population looking for work.

issues.name: Corruption
issues.blurb: Telecom and coal scandals in 2014, Rafale in 2019, electoral bonds and agency raids in 2024.

issues.name: National security
issues.blurb: The Mumbai attack, Pulwama and Balakot, and the border.

issues.name: Welfare and farm support
issues.blurb: Rural jobs guarantees, loan waivers, cash transfers and free grain.

issues.name: Growth and reform
issues.blurb: The Gujarat model, GST, demonetisation and who gets the jobs growth creates.

issues.name: Caste, religion and reservations
issues.blurb: Quotas, a caste census, the temple at Ayodhya and the citizenship law, as the parties raised them.

issues.name: Centre and states
issues.blurb: Telangana, special status for Andhra, tax shares and the powers of governors.

issues.name: Institutions and the Constitution
issues.blurb: Investigation agencies, the Election Commission, the courts and the question of changing the Constitution.

1999.label: 1999 · Vajpayee v. Sonia Gandhi
1999.tagline: September and October 1999. Vajpayee's government fell by a single vote in April, the Kargil war has just ended, and the NDA has gathered more than twenty parties behind him. Sonia Gandhi fights her first Lok Sabha election with few allies, and Sharad Pawar has left Congress over her Italian birth. Polling runs from 5 September to 3 October.

events.headline: Vajpayee's government fell by a single vote on 17 April when the AIADMK withdrew, and {party} asks voters to finish what the Lok Sabha could not
Sharad Pawar, P. A. Sangma and Tariq Anwar, expelled on 20 May for questioning Sonia Gandhi's Italian birth, have founded the NCP, and {party} fights Maharashtra against its own former chief minister
The DMK joins the NDA for the first time while the AIADMK, which brought the government down, stands with Congress in Tamil Nadu, and {party} gathers more than twenty parties
Sonia Gandhi files in Bellary as well as Amethi, and the BJP answers with Sushma Swaraj in Bellary, so {party} makes a southern seat the symbol of its campaign
In Andhra Pradesh the TDP takes 34 seats and the BJP 8 in one joint run against Congress, and {party} treats the state as its anchor in the south
Lalu Prasad Yadav is tied down at Madhepura by Sharad Yadav of the JD(U), and {party} has its Bihar chief fighting for his own seat
The Kargil war, ended in July, is still the story in every barracks town and village, and {party} campaigns on Vajpayee's handling of it
The BJP sets the 'videshi' Sonia Gandhi against the 'swadeshi' Vajpayee at every rally, and {party} has a ready contrast
Sonia Gandhi's offer in May to resign as party leader brought an outpouring of support, and {party} workers rally round her
Congress goes into the campaign with far fewer allies than the NDA's twenty-odd parties, and {party} has to win seat by seat on its own
Mulayam Singh Yadav refused in April to back a Sonia Gandhi government, and {party} now fights Congress as well as the BJP in Uttar Pradesh
The BSP contests every one of the 85 seats in Uttar Pradesh on its own, and {party} backs its Dalit base against all comers
Jayalalithaa's April suggestion of Jyoti Basu as prime minister, which he declined, keeps {party} in the national picture
Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress and the BJP take on the Left Front together across Bengal, and {party} faces a combined opposition in its stronghold
Steady growth and low inflation under the NDA give {party} a record to run on

issues.name: Kargil
issues.blurb: The war with Pakistan from May to July in the Kargil hills, and the Lahore bus journey that came before it.

issues.name: Sonia Gandhi's birth
issues.blurb: Her Italian birth, which three senior leaders cited when they left Congress to form the NCP, against Vajpayee.

issues.name: One vote
issues.blurb: The April confidence vote lost by one vote, and the third general election in under four years.

issues.name: Growth and reform
issues.blurb: Steady growth and low inflation under the NDA, and the pace of economic liberalisation.

issues.name: Jayalalithaa's cases
issues.blurb: The corruption cases against Jayalalithaa and her demand to dismiss the Tamil Nadu government, which brought the NDA down.

issues.name: Who allies with whom
issues.blurb: The NDA's twenty-odd parties, Congress's thin alliances and a loose Third Front of the Left and socialists.

issues.name: Temple and Christians
issues.blurb: The NDA agenda that left the temple and a uniform civil code aside, and the 1999 attacks on Christian missionaries.

2004.label: 2004 · Vajpayee v. Sonia Gandhi
2004.tagline: April and May 2004. The NDA has called the election early on the back of 'India Shining', a decisive run of state wins and a prime minister still ahead in the polls. Sonia Gandhi's Congress has finally built alliances in Tamil Nadu, Bihar and Maharashtra, while the Samajwadi Party and the BSP stand outside both fronts in Uttar Pradesh. Four phases of polling, counted on 13 May.

events.headline: The DMK and the PMK, who left the NDA in December and January over Ayodhya, have joined Congress's front in Tamil Nadu, and {party} faces a southern collapse
Rahul Gandhi announces in March that he will contest his father's old seat at Amethi, and {party} puts a new face in front of Uttar Pradesh
The BJP and the AIADMK tell the Election Commission they will keep raising Sonia Gandhi's foreign origin, and {party} spends another week on it
Vajpayee files his nomination at Lucknow on 7 April, and {party} opens its campaign on its best-known face
NDA leaders meet in New Delhi on 8 April to adopt an 'Agenda for Development and Good Governance', and {party} sets out the case for another term
Andhra Pradesh votes for the state assembly and the Lok Sabha together on 20 and 26 April, and {party}'s ally, the TDP, carries the weight of its time in office
Share prices start to fall after the second phase on 26 April as investors doubt an NDA win, and {party} is put on the defensive over its reform record
Booth capturing is reported at Chhapra in Bihar on 5 May and the Election Commission orders a fresh poll there, an awkward week for the RJD, {party}'s main Bihar ally
The 'India Shining' advertisements, reported at about 5 billion rupees, run in every medium while villages cope with drought, and {party} is accused of boasting
Talks with Congress collapsed, so Mulayam Singh Yadav's Samajwadi Party and its ally the RLD take on Congress, the BJP and the BSP alone, and {party} makes Uttar Pradesh a four-way race
Mayawati's BSP contests all 80 seats in Uttar Pradesh, and {party} bets on its Dalit base across the state
Karunanidhi's front of the DMK, Congress, PMK, MDMK and the Left puts up one candidate against the AIADMK and the BJP in each of Tamil Nadu's 39 seats, and {party} has a clear field
Lalu Prasad Yadav's RJD, Congress and Ram Vilas Paswan's LJP settle a Bihar seat deal of 26, 4 and 8, with one seat each for the NCP and the CPI(M), and {party} is the front to beat
Congress and the NCP fight Maharashtra as one front, with 26 and 18 seats, and {party} avoids the split vote that cost it in 1999
The Left Front fights Congress and the NDA in Bengal, Kerala and Tripura, and {party} presents itself as the vote that decides the next government

issues.name: India Shining
issues.blurb: Growth above 8 percent and the government's costly 'India Shining' advertising, set against villages that felt left out.

issues.name: Farm distress
issues.blurb: A poor 2002 monsoon, farm debt and farmers' suicides in Andhra Pradesh, against the boom in the cities.

issues.name: Ayodhya and Gujarat
issues.blurb: The Ram temple demand, which led the DMK and the PMK to leave the NDA, and the memory of the 2002 Gujarat riots.

issues.name: Vajpayee and Sonia Gandhi
issues.blurb: The prime minister's standing against Sonia Gandhi, whose foreign birth the BJP and the AIADMK kept raising.

issues.name: Jobs and disinvestment
issues.blurb: The sale of state companies and fears that growth was not creating jobs, a line the unions and the Left pressed.

issues.name: Terror and Pakistan talks
issues.blurb: The 2001 Parliament attack and the army standoff that followed, and the January 2004 peace talks with Pakistan.

issues.name: A stable government
issues.blurb: The NDA's closing argument: a single prime minister against a patchwork of parties that had never governed together.

issues.name: Water, roads and power
issues.blurb: Drought, water scarcity and bad roads and power in many states mattered more to voters than national themes.

2009.label: 2009 · Singh v. Advani
2009.tagline: April to May 2009. Manmohan Singh seeks a second term after the nuclear deal, the farm loan waiver and a global slump, and L. K. Advani makes his last run at the top job. The Left has withdrawn its support from the government, the Third Front is hunting for a leader, and Congress is fighting alone in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

events.headline: Naveen Patnaik ends eleven years of alliance with the BJP over seat sharing, and {party} goes to Odisha's voters on its own
Seat talks collapse and the SP, RJD and LJP form a fourth front, leaving Congress to fight alone in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. {party} has two big states to rebuild by itself
A hate speech case against Varun Gandhi, the BJP's candidate in Pilibhit, dominates the week, and {party} cannot shake it
A journalist throws a shoe at P. Chidambaram over the 1984 riot cases, and Congress drops Jagdish Tytler and Sajjan Kumar. {party} spends the week on the wrong story
Advani calls Manmohan Singh the weakest prime minister India has had, Singh replies with Advani's own record, and {party} spends days on the defensive
Jai Ho, the Oscar-winning song, becomes Congress's campaign anthem and blasts from every rally truck. {party} sounds like a winner from the start
The Mumbai attacks are still fresh, and the BJP campaigns hard on weak handling of terror. {party} gains with voters who want a tougher state
Singur and Nandigram have turned Bengal against its Left government, and the Trinamool and Congress alliance sweeps up the anger. {party} is the casualty
The 60,000 crore rupee farm loan waiver and the rural jobs guarantee are in every village conversation, and {party} claims the credit
Mayawati's name is floated as a Third Front prime minister, and {party} dreams big in Uttar Pradesh
Advani promises to bring back black money held in Swiss banks, and {party} finds a line that travels
Mulayam Singh Yadav's tie-up with Kalyan Singh, the former BJP chief minister, costs {party} Muslim votes
Jayalalithaa stitches together a front of the AIADMK, PMK, MDMK and the Left in Tamil Nadu, and {party} fights the DMK on even terms

issues.name: Loan waiver and NREGA
issues.blurb: The 2008 farm loan waiver of over 60,000 crore rupees and the rural jobs guarantee in every district.

issues.name: Terror after 26/11
issues.blurb: The November 2008 Mumbai attacks and the BJP's charge that the UPA was soft on terror.

issues.name: Global slowdown
issues.blurb: Growth down from 9 percent to under 7 after the 2008 crash, and job losses in exports.

issues.name: Price rise
issues.blurb: Food prices still climbing, though headline inflation fell from 12.9 percent in August 2008 to near zero.

issues.name: Communal politics
issues.blurb: Varun Gandhi's Pilibhit speech, the 2008 Kandhamal violence and the Ram temple in the BJP manifesto.

issues.name: Nuclear deal
issues.blurb: The civil nuclear agreement with the United States that cost Singh the Left's support in July 2008.

issues.name: Black money
issues.blurb: Advani's pledge to bring back Indian money held in Swiss banks, and the 2008 cash-for-votes scandal.

issues.name: Telangana demand
issues.blurb: The TRS demand for a separate Telangana state, which brought it into the TDP's grand alliance.

2014.label: 2014 · Modi v. Rahul Gandhi
2014.tagline: April to May 2014. Ten years of UPA rule are ending in scandal, price rises and policy drift, and the BJP has bet everything on one man, the Gujarat chief minister since 2001, Narendra Modi. A new party, the AAP, has just left the Delhi government to go national.

events.headline: Parliament carves out Telangana after pepper spray in the Lok Sabha, and {party} is blamed on both sides of the new border
Arvind Kejriwal quits as Delhi chief minister after 49 days and sets out to contest the country, and critics tell {party} it ran away
In January Mani Shankar Aiyar said Modi could come and serve tea at a Congress meeting, and {party} turns 'chaiwala' into its campaign
The Election Commission bars Amit Shah from rallies in Uttar Pradesh over a speech about 'revenge', and {party} spends a week answering for it
Modi files in Varanasi after a vast roadshow, with Kejriwal standing against him, and {party} owns the news cycle
Priyanka Gandhi attacks Modi's 'neech rajniti' and he turns the phrase into a charge of caste insult in his final rallies, and {party} loses the last argument
Telecom and coal scandals and a run of price rises have worn down the government's name, and {party} pays for ten years in office
Mulayam Singh Yadav says boys make mistakes of men facing the death penalty for rape, and {party} spends the week apologising
Jayalalithaa breaks with the Left and names candidates for all 40 seats on her own, and {party} runs as the only choice for a DMK-weary Tamil Nadu
Naveen Patnaik's handling of Cyclone Phailin, with few lives lost, is praised at home and abroad, and {party} rides the goodwill
Jagan Mohan Reddy runs on his father's welfare legacy across Andhra Pradesh, and {party} fills halls in every district
Modi's 3D hologram speeches reach hundreds of villages at once, and {party}'s message is everywhere in a single evening
The AAP's broom becomes the symbol of the anti-corruption mood in the cities, and {party} draws first-time voters
The Saradha chit fund collapse reaches the Bengal government's door, and {party} faces questions it would rather not answer

issues.name: Scams
issues.blurb: The 2G spectrum, coal block and Commonwealth Games scandals, and the Lokpal law passed in December 2013.

issues.name: Price rise
issues.blurb: Years of high food inflation, onions at 80 rupees a kilo in late 2013 and dearer diesel and gas.

issues.name: Development
issues.blurb: Growth below 5 percent, stalled projects and Modi's record as chief minister of Gujarat.

issues.name: Jobs for the young
issues.blurb: About 100 million first-time voters, and who could create work for them.

issues.name: Communal and caste politics
issues.blurb: The 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots, Modi's 2002 Gujarat record and caste arithmetic in UP and Bihar.

issues.name: Telangana
issues.blurb: The February law splitting Andhra Pradesh, and anger on both sides of the new border.

issues.name: Food security
issues.blurb: The National Food Security Act of 2013 and the rural jobs guarantee as Congress's record.

2019.label: 2019 · Modi v. Rahul Gandhi
2019.tagline: April to May 2019. A terror attack in Kashmir and an air strike across the border have turned the campaign into one about security, and Modi is asking for five more years. Congress has a minimum income promise, and in Uttar Pradesh the Samajwadi Party and the BSP have buried their feud.

events.headline: Parliament passes a 10 percent quota for economically weaker sections of the general category, and {party} shores up its upper-caste base
Mayawati and Akhilesh Yadav bury a decades-old feud and announce a joint front in Uttar Pradesh, and {party} sees its caste arithmetic add up
Forty CRPF men die at Pulwama and Indian jets strike Balakot twelve days later. Security displaces everything else, and {party} owns the moment
Rahul Gandhi promises 72,000 rupees a year to the poorest fifth of families under NYAY, and {party} finally has a number to sell
Rahul Gandhi files from Wayanad as well as Amethi. The Kerala seat lifts {party} in the south and hands its rival a line about running
Clashes break out at Amit Shah's roadshow in Kolkata and a Vidyasagar bust is smashed, and the Election Commission cuts the Bengal campaign short. {party} has made the state a national fight
Rahul Gandhi's 'chowkidar chor hai' attack on the Rafale deal meets Modi's 'main bhi chowkidar' reply, and {party} finds the charge has not travelled beyond its own supporters
The interim budget promises small farmers 6,000 rupees a year, and {party} answers the farm distress story with cash
Jagan Mohan Reddy ends a 3,600 kilometre walk across Andhra Pradesh, and {party} fills every hall it books
The Sabarimala temple dispute spills into Kerala politics, and {party} is blamed for enforcing the court's order
Naveen Patnaik reserves a third of BJD tickets for women, and {party} stands out in Odisha
Mamata Banerjee hosts opposition leaders from a dozen parties at a Kolkata rally, and {party} is cast as the architect of the anti-Modi front
The Election Commission bars Mayawati from campaigning for 48 hours over a speech to Muslim voters, and {party} loses days it cannot buy back

issues.name: Pulwama and Balakot
issues.blurb: The February bombing that killed 40 CRPF personnel and the air strike on Balakot that followed.

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: A leaked NSSO survey putting unemployment at 6.1 percent, a 45-year high, which the government disputed.

issues.name: Farmers and NYAY
issues.blurb: Low crop prices, PM-KISAN's 6,000 rupees a year to small farmers and Congress's NYAY income pledge.

issues.name: Rafale deal
issues.blurb: The 'chowkidar chor hai' charge over the fighter jet deal and the 'main bhi chowkidar' reply.

issues.name: Demonetisation and GST
issues.blurb: The 2016 note ban and the 2017 GST rollout: reform to some, a blow to small traders to others.

issues.name: Religion and citizenship
issues.blurb: The Ram temple dispute, the Citizenship Amendment Bill, a national citizens' register and the new EWS quota.

issues.name: Andhra special status
issues.blurb: Andhra Pradesh's demand for special category status, which took the TDP out of the NDA in 2018.

2024.label: 2024 · Modi v. Rahul Gandhi
2024.tagline: April to June 2024. Modi is asking for a third term and 'ab ki baar 400 paar', the Ram temple is open, and the opposition has built an INDIA bloc out of old rivals. An opposition chief minister is in custody, and the Hindi belt will say whether the BJP still wins without its allies.

events.headline: The Ram temple at Ayodhya is consecrated, and {party} carries the day's images into every village in the Hindi belt
Nitish Kumar quits the INDIA bloc he helped build and rejoins the NDA, and Mamata Banerjee says she will go alone in Bengal. {party} watches its alliance lose its first bricks
The Supreme Court strikes down electoral bonds and the list of donors is published, and {party} finds the cash trail dominating the week
The Enforcement Directorate arrests Arvind Kejriwal a month before polling opens, and {party} loses its best campaigner to a cell
Videos linked to Prajwal Revanna, the NDA's candidate in Hassan, surface days before Karnataka votes, and {party} spends the week disowning them
Opponents turn 'ab ki baar 400 paar' into a charge that the BJP needs 400 seats to change the Constitution, and {party}'s reservation message lands across the Hindi belt
Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra spends two months on the road through fifteen states, and {party} has a message for the villages
Anger over the short-service Agniveer recruitment scheme runs through army-recruiting districts in Haryana, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, and {party} takes the blame
The tax department freezes Congress bank accounts over old dues, and {party} starts the campaign short of cash
The TDP, Jana Sena and BJP seal a three-party pact in Andhra Pradesh, and {party} faces one united opponent for the first time
The BJP attacks the influence of V. K. Pandian, a Tamil-born former civil servant, over the BJD government in Odisha, and {party} struggles to answer
Allegations of land grabs and abuse against local Trinamool leaders in Sandeshkhali spread across Bengal, and {party} is forced onto the defensive
Both the Shiv Sena and the NCP have split, and the Uddhav Thackeray and Sharad Pawar factions must fight under new names. Maharashtra reads it as a grievance, and {party} benefits

issues.name: Unemployment
issues.blurb: Youth joblessness, leaked recruitment exam papers and the four-year Agnipath army scheme.

issues.name: Ram temple and religion
issues.blurb: The Ayodhya temple consecrated in January, and Modi's April speeches on Congress, wealth and Muslims.

issues.name: Save the Constitution
issues.blurb: Opposition claims that 400 seats would let the BJP rewrite the Constitution and end reservations.

issues.name: Price rise
issues.blurb: Food inflation near 8.7 percent in April and the cost of pulses, vegetables and cooking gas.

issues.name: Free ration and cash
issues.blurb: Free grain for 800 million people extended for five years, and Congress's pledge of 1 lakh a year to poor women.

issues.name: Caste census
issues.blurb: Rahul Gandhi's call for a national caste count after Bihar's 2023 survey, and the 50 percent quota cap.

issues.name: Electoral bonds and raids
issues.blurb: The Supreme Court striking down electoral bonds, and the arrests of Kejriwal and Hemant Soren.

issues.name: Viksit Bharat
issues.blurb: Modi's goal of a developed India by 2047, growth above 7 percent and new roads, railways and airports.

events.headline: A bad inflation print leads the evening bulletins, putting pressure on {party}
Onion and vegetable prices jump again, and voters look to {party}
A rally speech goes viral across the messaging apps, and {party} owns the day
An old video of a candidate resurfaces, and {party} spends the day explaining it
Seat arithmetic persuades smaller parties and local leaders to tilt toward {party}
{party}'s leader fumbles a question on prices in a television interview
Influential local leaders announce their support for {party}
A viral reel breaks for {party} among first-time voters
A long march through the villages wins {party} friendly local coverage
A heatwave on polling days thins the afternoon queues, and {party}'s organisation keeps its voters coming
A sitting MP crosses over to {party} on the eve of nominations
The Election Commission serves {party} a notice over a campaign speech
Floods put the administration to the test, and {party} looks the part
A national news channel offers {party} a long prime-time interview
events.prompt: The channel is not a friendly one, but the audience is enormous. How do you play it?

choices.text: Accept and take the hard questions
choices.resultText: You get through the rough patches and land a few lines that clip well. The overnight numbers move your way.

choices.text: Give it to a friendlier channel instead
choices.resultText: A comfortable hour. Your supporters cheer and nobody else changes their mind.

choices.text: Decline and let the rally crowds speak
choices.resultText: You skip the studio. The opposition fills the silence and calls it running away.

events.headline: Allies in a big state are haggling with {party} over who contests which seats
events.prompt: The deadline for nominations is Friday. What do you offer?

choices.text: Concede seats and keep the alliance whole
choices.resultText: The alliance holds, and your own workers grumble about the seats you gave up.

choices.text: Hold out for the seats you want
choices.resultText: You get most of what you asked for and a sulking ally.
A bold line that splits the vote. It also splits yours.

events.headline: {party}'s manifesto committee is split on the big welfare pledge
events.prompt: The manifesto goes to print on Friday. Which way do you push?

choices.text: Promise a large cash transfer or loan waiver
choices.resultText: The villages light up. Finance officials start sharpening pencils.

choices.text: Keep to schemes that are already funded
choices.resultText: No spark, and no self-inflicted wounds.

choices.text: Make it a contrast with the rival's record
choices.resultText: You define them more than yourself, and it lands.
